item.title: Current Events - September 30, 2026
item.description:
September 30, 2026 (2026-09-30) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Iraqi conflict
    • Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
      • American troops complete their withdrawal from Iraq, ending their 23-year presence in the country that started with the 2003 U.S. invasion, and also the 12-year U.S. intervention against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria. (AP) (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
    • A United States federal judge approves media conglomerate Paramount Skydance's settlement with 12 states that challenged its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on antitrust grounds, allowing the $81 billion merger to proceed toward completion. (AFP via ABS-CBN News)

Disasters and accidents

  • A helicopter crashes in Marondera, Zimbabwe, killing all six people on board, including businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife. (AFP via Daily Sun) (The Citizen)
  • Seven workers are killed in a gas incident inside a mining tunnel in Itogon, Benguet, Philippines. (Manila Bulletin)

Law and crime

  • Capital punishment in the United States
    • Capital punishment in Tennessee
      • The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit halts Christa Pike's execution in Tennessee shortly before it was scheduled, to allow for further review of whether evidence of childhood sexual abuse was adequately considered at sentencing; the U.S. Supreme Court shortly after lifts the Sixth Circuit's stay order, allowing the execution to proceed. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
      • Pike is sent to a hospital following the failed administration of two rounds of the drugs used to perform the lethal injection. (Axios) (BBC News)
  • 2026 Turkish LGBTQ raids, Censorship in Turkey, Censorship of LGBTQ issues
    • A Turkish court orders the closure of independent news website T24 and its social media accounts after the justice ministry reported that T24 had published 118 items during the previous year which the court classified as "LGBTQ propaganda". (AFP via RTL Today)
  • Flydubai Flight 1073
    • A Flydubai flight from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, to Tel Aviv, Israel, is landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, by a relief crew after the copilot violently attacked the captain in an attempted aircraft hijacking. (BBC News) (CNN)
  • Narcotics in Bolivia
    • Bolivian police arrest attorney general Roger Mariaca and Santa Cruz de la Sierra prosecutor Alberto Zeballos after the U.S. State Department accused them of corruption and links to drug trafficking. Police also raid prosecutors' offices in several cities. (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Romanian political crisis
    • Romania's parliament rejects prime minister-designate Siegfried Mureșan's proposed government, receiving 182 of the 233 votes required for approval, prolonging the political crisis that began after Ilie Bolojan's government fell in May. (AFP) (AP)
  • At least 450 people are arrested and 76 people are injured after students in France protest over class overcrowding and teacher shortages. (BBC News) (The New York Times)

Science and technology

  • AI boom
    • The Tokyo District Court rules that a person's voice can receive protection under publicity rights, in Japan's first case involving alleged audio deepfake, while dismissing actor Kenjiro Tsuda's request to remove already-deleted TikTok videos. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - October 07, 2026
item.description:
October 7, 2026 (2026-10-07) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Houthi forces claim attacks on Abha International Airport and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia that killed three civilians and injured 36 others since yesterday. (AFP via France 24)
    • Israeli settler violence
      • Israeli settlers launch an attack in the occupied West Bank targeting Palestinians, killing a man and wounding 16 other people. (Al Jazeera)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • 2026 Eritrean invasion of Ethiopia
        • Eritrean forces are reported to have invaded Ethiopia's Tigray Region and are moving south toward Mekelle. (Addis Standard) (Al Jazeera)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russian forces launch a massive ballistic missile and drone attack on Ukraine, killing at least 28 people, including 20 people killed at a single apartment hit by a North Korean KN-23 missile in Pryluky, Chernihiv Oblast, while hundreds more are wounded. (The Guardian)
    • Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Bulgaria halts the search for the 12 Syrian sailors missing since yesterday after a merchant ship sank after being hit by a drone strike in its waters. The perpetrators are still unknown. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • Mali War
    • 2026 Mali offensives
      • The Malian Armed Forces and the Russian Africa Corps retake Kidal, which was captured by the Azawad Liberation Front five months ago, after days of airstrikes and ground operations. (Al Jazeera)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • 2026 Blue Nile campaign
      • Four women are killed in a Rapid Support Forces drone strike on homes and a mosque in Ad-Damazin, Blue Nile State, Sudan. (The Washington Post) (AP)

Business and economy

  • Guinea sets nationwide price ceilings for bottled water after a ban on single-use plastic water sachets causes shortages and higher prices, with retail packs of several bottle sizes capped at 25,000 francs (US$2.84). (AFP via France 24)
  • The Reserve Bank of India raises its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, its first increase since February 2023. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Hurricane Isaias
      • Tropical cyclone Isaias strengthens into a category 1 hurricane, becoming the first Atlantic hurricane of the season amidst a unusually quiet season caused by the ongoing El Niño phenomenon. (AP)
      • In the United States, Alabama governor Kay Ivey declares a state of emergency for 40 counties ahead of Isaias. (Reuters) (WVUA-CD)

Health and environment

  • Climate change in Antarctica
    • The British Antarctic Survey reports that Zavodovski Island in Antarctica has lost more than 500,000 chinstrap penguins since 2011, ending its status as the world's largest penguin colony as warming waters reduce access to Antarctic krill. (AFP via France 24)
  • Climate change in Australia, Mining in Australia
    • Australia's High Court rejects MACH Energy's appeal to expand the Mount Pleasant coal mine in New South Wales, finding that planning authorities failed to adequately consider greenhouse gas emissions from burning exported coal overseas. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Elections in Mexico
    • Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum sanctions a constitutional amendment prohibiting Mexicans with dual citizenship from running for president or governor. (AA) (El Economista in Spanish)
  • International spillover of the 2026 French lycée protests
    • For a second consecutive day, riots occur in Liège, Belgium, following earlier student protests, prompting authorities to close the Guillemins railway station and urge local businesses to shut down. Over 100 people are arrested. (Al Jazeera) (RTBF)
  • Libor scandal
    • The Court of Appeal in London, United Kingdom, quashes the convictions of five former Barclays traders for manipulating Libor and Euribor, following a 2025 Supreme Court ruling that found legal errors had made similar convictions unsafe. (AFP)
  • School attacks in Poland
    • Nine people are injured in a mass stabbing at a high school in Ostrołęka, Poland. The suspect, a 19-year-old student, is arrested after being injured himself. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • French chemist Henri B. Kagan from the Paris-Saclay University and Japanese organic chemist Kensō Soai from the Tokyo University of Science are jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for "the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis". (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - September 29, 2026
item.description:
September 29, 2026 (2026-09-29) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Gaza war
    • Israeli settler violence, Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
      • More than 100 Israeli settlers attack the Palestinian village of Jalud in the occupied West Bank, burning two homes and injuring three Israeli security personnel while preventing a displaced Palestinian family from returning home. (AFP via The Manila Times)
    • An Israeli airstrike kills Izz al-Din al-Beik, the head of Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades in the northern Gaza Strip. (Reuters)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Piracy off the coast of Somalia, Anti-piracy measures, Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
      • The Puntland Maritime Police Force successfully frees another hijacked oil tanker, the MT Honour ​25, following an ongoing week-long counter-piracy operation near Bayla, Karkaar, Puntland, after it was seized by Somali pirates on 21 April ​around 30 nautical miles off Puntland's coast with 17 crew members on board. (Reuters) (Somali Guardian)
      • Five crew members aboard the MT Honour 25 are killed and four more injured by the pirates before the rescue. The victims are three citizens of Pakistan and one each from India and Myanmar. It is the first time in over a decade that people are killed by the pirates. (Al Jazeera)

Arts and culture

  • The coronation ceremony for Nyabongo I of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom is held, formally making him king. (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • The Reserve Bank of Australia raises its cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.60%, the highest level since 2011, citing persistently high inflation above its 2–3% target range. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
  • Julius Baer Group controversies
    • The Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) concludes its investigation into the Julius Baer Group, finding serious risk-management and anti–money laundering failures. FINMA orders additional capital requirements, compliance reporting through 2032, and the confiscation of about CHF10 million (US$12 million) in profits. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • A vehicle crashes through a fence and plunges into the River Wear in Sunderland, Tyne and Wear, England, killing three teenagers. The driver of the vehicle, also a teenager, is later arrested by Northumbria Police. (Sky News)

Health and environment

  • The Japan Meteorological Agency reports rainfall in Tokyo for 34 consecutive days through today, the longest streak since records began in 1886 and one day longer than the previous record set in 2019. (AFP via France 24) (Bloomberg)
  • The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issues two recalls for more than 25,000 bottles of chlorthalidone, a diuretic antihypertensive drug, created by Indian-based Inventia Healthcare Limited, due to faulty dissolution times in the human body. (USA Today)

International relations

  • North Korea–South Korea relations
    • Korean conflict
      • South Korean defense minister Kang Shin-chul says that land mines planted by North Korea likely caused two explosions last week that injured three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone south of the military demarcation line, potentially violating the armistice. (AFP via RFI)
  • Haitian crisis
    • The United Nations Security Council extends the mandate of the Gang Suppression Force in Haiti by six months, allowing the multinational force to continue supporting Haitian security forces against armed gangs. (AFP via RFI)
  • Malaysia–Myanmar relations, Myanmar civil war
    • Malaysia begins repatriating about 1,500 Burmese nationals from immigration detention centres under the first phase of a programme covering 5,000 people. (AFP via RTL Today)

Law and crime

  • Myanmar civil war
    • Twenty-one people are arrested in Myanmar for allegedly donating to the in-exile National Unity Government-linked People's Revolution Supply Family fundraising platform as the government identifies more than 2,700 alleged contributors. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Staškov school stabbing
    • A teacher is killed and a student and another teacher are wounded in a mass stabbing at a secondary school in Staškov, Slovakia. The perpetrator, a fellow student, is arrested. (Euronews)
  • Crime in Mexico
    • The Supreme Court of Mexico invalidates the state of Chihuahua's authority to annul elections due to interference by organized crime and instructs the local legislature to instead include the annulment of elections due to foreign interference. (El Sol de México)
  • Seventeen people are arrested during a security operation involving 800 police officers against a "suspected organised crime group" in five cities in the United Kingdom, including London. A police officer is stabbed and wounded during one of the raids. (Sky News)
  • The Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park in Valencia, California, U.S., announces that the X2 roller coaster will close permanently after several lawsuits alleged that over 100 riders sustained brain injuries while riding the attraction. (BBC)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Moroccan general election
    • King Mohammed VI appoints Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the first female prime minister of Morocco after her victory in the general elections on 23 September. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games, South Korea at the 2026 Asian Games
      • In badminton, South Korea's An Se-young wins the women's singles gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games, becoming the first woman to win two singles titles and the first to defend the title, defeating Japan's Akane Yamaguchi 21–17, 21–9. (AFP via RFI)
  • Manchester City F.C. financial breaches scandal
    • In association football, an independent Premier League commission finds Manchester City guilty of almost all 115-plus financial charges, including inflating revenue by more than £900 million (US$1.19 billion) and failing to cooperate with the investigation. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - October 06, 2026
item.description:
October 6, 2026 (2026-10-06) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • The Houthis launches missiles against the airports of Najran and Jizan, in Saudi Arabia, causing material damages and wounding three people. (Al Jazeera)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli defense minister Israel Katz says that the military has killed 4,000 militants who took part in the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023. (The Jewish Chronicle)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Piracy off the coast of Somalia
      • Four Indonesian seamen return home after Puntland maritime police rescued 17 crew members from the hijacked oil tanker MT Honour 25. Somali pirates had held the crew for more than five months and killed five members. (AFP)
  • Peruvian security crisis
    • Three gunmen and a police officer are killed, and another officer is wounded, in a shootout during an operation against illegal miners in Inambari District, Tambopata province, Madre de Dios, Peru. Authorities seize 15 AKM rifles, a pistol, and five grenades. (Evidencia de Perú in Spanish) (Infobae in Spanish)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)
      • Two merchant ships are hit by drones of unknown origins off the coast of Bulgaria. One of the ships has sunk, leaving the crew missing. (Reuters)
  • At least ten soldiers are killed by Islamic State gunmen during an attack at a military base in Kukawa, Borno State, Nigeria. Over 25 attackers are also killed in the shootout. (AP)

Business and economy

  • Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount
    • The merger between American media conglomerates Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery into Skydance takes effect. (AFP) (CNN)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • Kenya confirms its first imported case of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebolavirus in Nairobi in a deceased male who traveled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. (Reuters)
    • The Nairobi Hospital steps up its infection-control measures, tracing, and staff monitoring following Kenya's first imported case of Ebola. (The Star Kenya)
  • Indonesia halts a program to clear millions of hectares of forest for rice cultivation after achieving rice self-sufficiency, and plans instead to increase yields on existing farmland through improved agricultural methods. (AFP via CNA)

Law and crime

  • Spillover of the 2026 French lycée protests
    • Riots break out in Liège, Belgium, following a day of student protests, resulting in damaged shops and destroyed bus shelters in the city center. (AA) (Le Soir)
  • August Hanning, former head of Germany's Federal Intelligence Service, is arrested at his home in Nordwalde, North Rhine-Westphalia, after being charged by the country's Federal Public Prosecutor General with treason, espionage, and trading state secrets. A former aide of Hanning's is also arrested for aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage. (AP) (DW)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Haitian general election, Haitian crisis
    • Haiti's Provisional Electoral Council postpones presidential and legislative elections scheduled for December 13, citing technical, operational, and security requirements. (AFP)
  • 2026 Kosovan presidential election
    • The Kuvendi begins the procedure to elect a president on 6 October, finishing the voting process minutes after the constitutional deadline on midnight 7 October. Justina Pula is declared the next president of Kosovo. (AFP via Gulf News) (Kosovo Online)

Science and technology

  • 2026 in archosaur paleontology
    • The Royal Society Open Science reports the discovery of the Herugavialis cairensis crocodile species in the Mokattam Formation rocks that were used to build the Great Sphinx Giza pyramid in Egypt. (CNN) (Phys.org)
  • Mathematics and artificial intelligence, List of mathematical discoveries by artificial intelligence
    • OpenAI releases 377 results on open problems in mathematics in areas such as algebra, number theory, combinatorics and theoretical computer science. (The New York Times)
  • Belgian physicist Francis Halzen from the University of Wisconsin–Madison is awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his "decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin". (CNN)

item.title: Current Events - October 08, 2026
item.description:
October 8, 2026 (2026-10-08) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East
        • The USS Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego, California, U.S., at the North Island Naval Air Station following its nearly seven-month deployment in the Middle East. (The Guardian) (Los Angeles Times)
      • U.S. president Donald Trump says that the U.S. military will not attack Iran before the midterm elections next month. (AP)
    • Gaza war
      • Gaza war hostage crisis
        • The Israel Defense Forces announce that they have killed Muhammad Muhsen Nimr Yazji, a Hamas militant who took part in holding Emily Damari, Romi Gonen, and Matan Angrest during an airstrike in Gaza City. (The Jerusalem Post)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russian forces launch a ballistic missile attack on two buses in the city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine, killing at least 30 people, while 18 others are wounded. (Al Jazeera)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Ten inmates are killed and 16 more injured during a prison riot in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico. (AP)

Arts and culture

  • 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
    • Canadian poet Anne Carson is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for "her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms ‌for contemporary literature". (BBC News)
  • The Bank of England announces that the Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee, and European hedgehog will feature on the next set of pound sterling notes to be issued in the United Kingdom. It will be the first time animals have replaced people on banknotes in England, which is intended to increase awareness of British wildlife. (BBC News)

Business and economy

  • AI boom, Semiconductor industry in Taiwan
    • The Taiwanese finance ministry reports that exports reached a record US$87.2 billion in September, while imports rose to a record $63.6 billion and the trade surplus reached a record $23.6 billion, citing demand for artificial intelligence-related hardware. (AFP) (Reuters)
  • The Hungarian newspaper Népszabadság, which was shut down in 2016 during the government of former prime minister Viktor Orbán, relaunches as an online news site. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Hurricane Isaias
      • In the United States, Georgia governor Brian Kemp declares a state of emergency ahead of Hurricane Isaias. (Fox 5 Atlanta)
      • Hurricane Isaias strengthens into a category 2 Atlantic hurricane. (AP)
  • Severe rainfall in Chile, particularly in Santiago, caused flooding, river overflowing, mudslides, and power outages, killing one person, injuring six others and damaging over 2,000 homes. (NBC News)

International relations

  • South Korea–Ukraine relations, North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war
    • South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine after accusing Ukraine of breaching a non-disclosure agreement by disclosing the transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea. (AFP via The Straits Times)

Law and crime

  • 2009 Fort Hood shooting, Capital punishment in the United States
    • United States secretary of defense Pete Hegseth announces the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, will be publicly broadcast. (AFP via RFI) (CNN)
  • 2026 Poland school stabbings
    • A 15-year-old student carries out a mass stabbing against staff members at a primary school in the village of Leszczydół-Nowiny, Wyszków County, Poland, killing one person and injuring two more. The suspect is taken into police custody. (Reuters)
  • Relationship of Prince Andrew and Jeffrey Epstein
    • High Court judge Nicholas Hilliard of England and Wales quashes search warrants used on Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes, finding errors in Thames Valley Police's applications and issuing judge Mark Lucraft's consideration of legally protected material. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • Next Guinea-Bissau general election
    • The Government of Guinea-Bissau announces that presidential and parliamentary elections scheduled for December 6 will be delayed. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Nippon Professional Baseball season
    • In baseball, Teruaki Satō of the Hanshin Tigers wins the Triple Crown. (Kyodo News)
  • 2026 WNBA season
    • In women's basketball, Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson wins a record fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player, becoming the first player in league history to win the award for three years in a row. (ESPN)
  • Swiss and Sunderland A.F.C. footballer Granit Xhaka receives a two-year probation after admitting to obtaining a fake COVID-19 vaccination certificate during the COVID-19 pandemic. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - October 01, 2026
item.description:
October 1, 2026 (2026-10-01) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Iraqi conflict
    • Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
      • Ahmad al-Hamidawi, leader of Kata'ib Hezbollah, announces that the group will suspend military activities in Iraq following the withdrawal of U.S. troops, with the exception of targeting hostile aircraft violating the country's airspace. (Middle East Eye)
  • Israeli–Palestinian conflict
    • Israeli settler violence, Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
      • Israeli settlers shoot and kill a Palestinian man at his home in Yasuf, West Bank, and injure another. (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Aviation shootdowns and accidents during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Russian Su-35 fighter jet shoots down a Russian Mi-8 helicopter over Voronezh Oblast, Russia, in a friendly fire incident. All three crew members are killed. (Kyiv Independent)
  • Sudanese civil war, Kordofan campaign
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces on a dormitory at the University of Kordofan in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, kills five people. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • Explosions caused by suspected drone strikes are reported in Ethiopia's capital of Addis Ababa, including one near the Ethiopian National Defense Force' headquarters. (BBC News)
  • 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
    • Pakistan launches airstrikes in Afghanistan, claiming the killing of 22 Taliban fighters at two locations, while the Government of Afghanistan reports that nine women and children are killed in Kunar Province and Helmand Province by Pakistan airstrikes. (Al Jazeera)

Disasters and accidents

  • A medical helicopter transporting a patient crashes off the coast of Santa Catalina Island in Los Angeles County, California, United States, killing two people, injuring two others, and leaving one missing. (AP)

International relations

  • Ethiopian civil conflict, TPLF insurgency in Ethiopia
    • Eritrea–Ethiopia relations
      • Ethiopia closes its embassy in Eritrea and announces the expulsion of ten Eritrean diplomats from the country, after accusing its neighbour of financing the Tigray People's Liberation Front. (AP)
      • Eritrea's foreign ministry announces that the country will cut off diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in response. (AFP via Al Arabiya) (Reuters)
    • Egypt–Ethiopia relations
      • A diplomat from Egypt is told to leave Ethiopia within 48 hours after being declared as persona non grata. (Reuters)
  • The European Commission stops payments with immediate effect to Sierra Leone, which would have been €18 million for 2026, after the nation refused to cooperate with the extradition of drugs trafficker Jos Leijdekkers. (Het Parool)

Law and crime

  • Censorship in Egypt, Human rights in Egypt
    • Egyptian police are arresting six journalists from a fact-checking and investigative media outlet, accusing them of spreading misinformation on behalf of the banned Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt. (Reuters)
  • 2026 RAF Fairford arrests
    • British counter-terrorism police arrest a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national in Westminster, London, England, on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts linked to the RAF Fairford investigation. Officers also search two properties in the area. (CNN)
  • Sentencing Act 2026
    • Hundreds of prisoners begin leaving prison in England and Wales under an early release scheme by the British government to avoid overcapacity in prisons. More than 4,500 "low-risk" prisoners are expected to be released in the coming weeks. (BBC News) (Firstpost)
  • Former Malawian military chief Paul Valentino Phiri is arrested by Malawi's anti-corruption agency for allegedly trafficking weapons to Sudan during his tenure in June and July 2025. (Al-Monitor)
  • Two 18-year-old former students attack a secondary school in Torreón, Coahuila, Mexico, with knives and pyrotechnic devices, killing the vice-principal and injuring three people. Police arrest both suspects. (AFP via RNZ)

Politics and elections

  • Immigration to Japan
    • Japan tightens permanent residency requirements for foreign nationals, introducing above-average income and basic Japanese-language standards while raising application fees twentyfold as part of broader changes to immigration policy. (AFP)
  • Gerardo Giovagnoli and William Casali are sworn in as the new Captains Regent of San Marino, succeeding Alice Mina and Vladimiro Selva. (San Marino RTV)
  • Ousted Sudanese leader Omar al-Bashir is sent to a military hospital in Khartoum, Sudan, for medical treatment. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • SpaceX Crew-13
    • The SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station launches, carrying two NASA astronauts, one Roscosmos cosmonaut, and one Canadian Space Agency astronaut, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, United States. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - October 11, 2026
item.description:
October 11, 2026 (2026-10-11) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • October 2026 attacks on Saudi Arabia airports
          • Houthis launch an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, causing a fire, killing one person and injuring multiple people. (Sky News) (Al Jazeera)
          • An Indian national injured in yesterday's attack on King Khalid International Airport dies from his injuries, raising the total death toll to 13. (Reuters)
        • The Royal Saudi Air Force launches an airstrike in Sanaa, Yemen, killing a child and wounding seven other people. (Al Jazeera)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reports that a tanker transiting in the Strait of Hormuz has been hit by an unknown projectile. (Middle East Eye)
        • A drone strikes the Nicaragua-flagged tanker MT Petro Dolphin near Sohar, Oman, leaving two Indian sailors missing and prompting the rescue of nine others. Omani authorities conduct search-and-rescue operations for the missing crew members. (AFP via Arab News)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • Airstrikes are launched at the Egypt–Sudan border targeting an artisanal gold mine in a mountainous area, killing at least 72 people. (Sky News)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Three civilians and two police officers are killed in a mass shooting in Jacona, Michoacán, Mexico, while six other people are wounded. Separately, three gunmen are killed in a shootout with police in Zamora. (OEM in Spanish)
  • Colombian conflict
    • Four FARC dissidents are killed and 12 rifles seized after an airstrike by the National Army of Colombia against a guerrilla camp in Norte de Santander Department, Colombia. (El Tiempo in Spanish)
    • A drone strike kills a soldier in La Vega, Cauca Department, Colombia. (Publimetro)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Budhi Gandaki flood
    • Ten people are reported missing and at least 35 houses and six bridges are swept away in a major flash flood in Gorkha District, Gandaki Province, Nepal. The exact number of casualties is unknown. (ANI via Gulf News) (Nepal Views)
  • At least 139 people are killed, 84 more are missing, and over 80 are rescued when a boat carrying migrants shipwrecks off the coast of Djibouti. (AFP via France 24)
  • Eleven people are killed and 27 others are injured when a tour bus collides with a truck at a toll road of Otoyol 5 in Akhisar, Manisa Province, Turkey. (Türkiye Today)
  • One person is killed and around 19 others are injured, including four critically, when a passenger bus plunges down a slope and crashes into a residential complex in Valparaíso, Chile. (Teletrece in Spanish)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Kenyan health ministry reports that no Ebola cases have been reported since one patient died from the disease on October 5, with 293 tests conducted. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • The Indonesian forestry ministry and International Animal Rescue release eight orangutans rescued from wildfires into a protected wildforest in West Kalimantan after fires destroyed habitat near plantations. (AFP)

Law and crime

  • 2026 anti-CEC protests
    • An executive magistrate's court in New Delhi, India, orders the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders, requiring them to avoid breaches of the peace for one year after their detention. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa state of emergency
    • Pakistani president Asif Ali Zardari declares a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspends its provincial government amid disputes over the province's response to Islamist militancy. (AFP via RFI)
  • 2027 French presidential election
    • Raphaël Glucksmann is elected as a candidate in the 2027 presidential election during the Socialist Party primary, receiving more than 66% of the votes in the first round. (AFP via RFI)
  • 2026 Kraków mayoral election
    • Independent candidate Łukasz Gibała wins the Kraków mayoral election in Poland against government-backed Civic Platform senator Monika Piątkowska.(Politico)

item.title: Current Events - October 04, 2026
item.description:
October 4, 2026 (2026-10-04) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • Ethiopian forces capture Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray Region, after the withdrawal of the Tigray People's Liberation Front. (Al Jazeera)
      • A drone strikes a displacement camp in Sheraro, Tigray Region, killing at least eight people, including a child, and seriously injuring six others. (AFP via France 24)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war, Kordofan campaign
      • The World Food Programme reports an airstrike on a United Nations truck in South Kordofan, Sudan, that killed the driver. (Al Jazeera)
  • War on cartels
    • United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
      • Four people are killed in an American airstrike against an alleged drug boat in the Caribbean Sea. (AP)
  • Yemeni civil war
    • 2026 Yemen offensives
      • The Houthis take control of Al-Turbah, Yemen, after government troops withdrew earlier in the day. This is the first time the Houthis have held Al-Turbah since the war began. (Yemen Online) (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • The United States Coast Guard suspends the search for the Latitude Air Ambulance Gulfstream G100 aircraft that went missing yesterday with six passengers on board after finding a debris field in the ocean south of Nantucket, Massachussetts. All six passengers, including four Canadian pilots and crew and two Bermudian passengers, are presumed dead. (CBC) (Winnipeg City News)

Health and environment

  • A lab worker in Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute in Shelekhov, Irkutsk Oblast, Siberia, dies from a pneumonic plague caused by Yersinia pestis, with nearly 200 workers in quarantine. (EuroWeekly News) (Kyiv Independent)

International relations

  • Nicaragua announces its immediate withdrawal from the Central American Parliament after the Organization of American States approved a resolution on Friday calling for Nicaragua to release political prisoners and restore civil liberties. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Vienna, Georgia, shooting
    • Two people are killed and at least 35 are injured in a mass shooting during a homecoming block party in Vienna, Georgia, United States. (AP) (The Guardian)
  • Chinese espionage in the United States
    • The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation arrests a 34-year-old Chinese American woman at Los Angeles International Airport in California for allegedly acting as an unregistered Chinese agent and surveilling Taiwanese president Lai Ching-te's son and family in the United States. (AFP via RFI) (The Daily Telegraph)
  • Two people are killed and another is injured in a mass shooting at a hunting party in Halden, Norway. The perpetrator is arrested. (AP)
  • An American Marine stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Ginowan, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan, is arrested by Okinawa prefectural police in connection with the alleged robbery and murder of a local woman in Naha. Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi summons U.S. ambassador to Japan George Edward Glass regarding the incident. (NPR)
  • Three students are arrested for the murder of a 16-year-old classmate in Yong Peng, Johor, Malaysia. (The Straits Times)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Bosnian general election
    • Bosnians vote to elect the three members of the presidency and 42 members of the House of Representatives. Concurrent elections are also held in the Federation to elect 98 seats of the regional legislature and in Republika Srpska to elect the entity's president and the 83 seats of the respective legislature. (AFP)
  • 2026 Brazilian general election
    • Brazilians head to the polls to elect their president, vice president, 513 members of Chamber of Deputies and 54 members in the Federal Senate. Incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is running for the fourth non-consecutive term, where his main opponent is Rio de Janeiro senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. (The Guardian)
    • Flávio Bolsonaro wins the first round and will face Lula da Silva in a runoff on 25 October. (AP)

Sports

  • 2034 FIFA World Cup
    • It is reported that Saudi Arabia has cancelled plans for the proposed NEOM Stadium in The Line, Neom, for the upcoming 2034 FIFA World Cup in the country. (Middle East Eye) (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - October 10, 2026
item.description:
October 10, 2026 (2026-10-10) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • 2026 Eritrean incursion into Ethiopia
        • Ethiopian forces regain control of Adigrat in the Tigray Region following a withdrawal of Eritrean forces. Celebrations are reported in the city following the withdrawal. (Oman Observer) (Al Jazeera) (UA News)
  • Yemeni civil war
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict
      • October 2026 King Khalid International Airport attack
        • Twelve people are killed and 309 more injured in a Houthi missile attack against Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (The Wall Street Journal) (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Zaporizhzhia strikes
      • At least 20 people are killed and 18 others are injured in a Russian airstrike on a five-story residential building in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine. (Ukrainska Pravda)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • The National Hurricane Center reports that Hurricane Isaias has weakened to a post-tropical cyclone after making landfall near Destin, Florida, United States. (WVTM-TV) (NBC News)
    • Four people are killed during Isaias' landfall in the United States, with two deaths in Escambia County, Florida, and another two in Alabama. (The Guardian)
  • 2026 Pacific hurricane season
    • Tropical storm Simon strengthens into a category 4 Pacific hurricane with 150 mph (240 kph) winds as it heads towards Mexico's coast. (AP) (The Rio Times)
  • A man is killed after jumping into a tiger enclosure and being attacked at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in South Yorkshire, England. The tiger was uninjured. (BBC News)

Law and crime

  • Censorship in India
    • 2026 anti-CEC protests
      • Indian authorities are placing New Delhi under a security lockdown and have been detaining thousands of demonstrators to block a rally organized by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party. (BBC News) (The Guardian) (The New York Times)
  • 2026 Poland school stabbings
    • A woman carries out a mass stabbing at an adult school in Warsaw, Poland, injuring three people. The suspect is arrested. It is the third such attack in the country in a week. (AP)

Sports

  • 2026–27 La Liga
    • In association football, the match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Bilbao is abandoned by referee José María Sánchez Martínez due to fans throwing objects at the pitch to protest against Rayo president Raúl Martín Presa. (Reuters)
  • 2026 NCAA Division I FBS football season
    • In American college football, the Kentucky Wildcats football team defeats the LSU Tigers 35–34 on a 2-point conversion in overtime, becoming the first team in FBS history to win consecutive overtime games by one point since overtime was introduced in 1996. (The Athletic via The New York Times) (The Score)
  • 2026 Il Lombardia
    • In cycling, French cyclist Paul Seixas wins the 120th edition of the Giro di Lombardia in Italy, becoming the youngest person to do so. (NBC Sports) (The Guardian)

item.title: Current Events - October 03, 2026
item.description:
October 3, 2026 (2026-10-03) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Iraq's Oil Tankers Company says that they have transported 2 million barrels of oil from the country through a very large crude carrier in the Strait of Hormuz. (Reuters) (Arab News)
    • Gaza war
      • Gaza genocide
        • Five people are killed and several more are injured in an Israeli airstrike against a residential building in Gaza City, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. Three other Palestinians are also killed in more airstrikes. (Al Jazeera)
      • The Israel Defense Forces says that they have targeted defacto Hamas leader Ali al-Amoudi in a airstrike, and acknowledge that the results of the strike are under review. (The Times of Israel)
    • Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
      • Unknown gunmen open fire against a vehicle in Ras al-Maara, Syria, killing three people and wounding seven more. (Hawar News Agency)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • Ethiopian federal forces retake control of the Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle, Tigray, from the Tigray People's Liberation Front. (Los Angeles Times)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
      • Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko reports that Russian forces have struck the Pivnichnyi Bridge in Kyiv, Ukraine. (Kyiv Independent)

Arts and culture

  • The remains of Samuel, the former Bulgarian tsar during the First Bulgarian Empire who died in 1014, return to Bulgaria following decades of negotiation with Greece. (Orthodox Times) (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • Ten people are injured, including some critically, in an motor vehicle hooning incident in Newcastle, Australia, during a Newcastle Knights procession before the NRL Grand Final. The driver is arrested at the scene. The incident is considered unintentional. (Nine News)
  • A Latitude Air Ambulance Gulfstream G100, flying from St. David's Island, Bermuda to Boston, United States, goes missing over the Atlantic Ocean with six people on board. Search operations are ongoing. (News 18)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Latvian parliamentary election
    • Latvians vote to elect 100 seats of the Saeima amid an uptick of airspace incursions and hybrid warfare during the Russo-Ukrainian war. Preliminary results indicate that the centrist United List, led by incumbent prime minister Andris Kulbergs, won the most seats. (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - October 12, 2026
item.description:
October 12, 2026 (2026-10-12) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Business and economy

  • 2026 Nobel Prizes
    • American economists Robert Ernest Hall and Michael Dean Woodford are jointly awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for "microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation". (CNN)

Disasters and accidents

  • A fire destroys the historic Marché des Enfants Rouges food market in Paris, France. (France 24)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Aubagne school shooting
    • A 14-year-old student opens fire at a middle school in Aubagne, France, injuring two staff members, before being detained. (France24)
  • 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa state of emergency
    • Pakistan's federal government detains hundreds of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) members, including former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi and other provincial officials, after suspending the PTI-led provincial administration and imposing emergency rule. (AFP via RFI)
  • The criminal trial of Russell Brand on charges of rape and sexual assault begins with jury selection. (BBC)
  • A cyber attack without attribution against French supermarkets results in losses worth millions of euros. (BBC)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Estonian presidential election
    • Ülle Madise, who was elected by the Riigikogu last 2 September, takes office as President of Estonia, succeeding Alar Karis. (Estonian World)

item.title: Current Events - October 05, 2026
item.description:
October 5, 2026 (2026-10-05) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Yemeni civil war
    • 2026 Yemen offensives, Operation Dawn of Yemen
      • The Presidential Leadership Council launches a large-scale military operation against Houthis in Yemen, with the aim to capture all Houthi-controlled territories. (Al Arabiya) (Al Jazeera) (TRT World)
      • Turkey and Pakistan agree to deploy troops under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement to help Saudi and Yemeni forces against the Houthis. (Al Jazeera)
      • A Yemeni government offensive pushes the Houthis back from the Bab al-Mandab Strait. (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Brazilian general election
    • Brazil's benchmark Ibovespa index rises nearly 9% to almost 210,000 points after the first round of the presidential election, surpassing 200,000 points for the first time. (AFP via France 24)
  • Russian president Vladimir Putin approves the restructuring of UniCredit Bank Russia and the subsequent sale of most of the business to a United Arab Emirates-based private investor, while UniCredit retains its payments operations. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Nigerian Air Force ATR 42 crash
    • A Nigerian Air Force ATR 42-500 aircraft crashes in Ondo State, Nigeria, killing all 25 people on board. (DW) (Reuters)
  • The toll from yesterday's collision between two ships in the Congo River near Lukolela, Democratic Republic of the Congo, increases to 30 people killed and dozens missing. (AP)

International relations

  • United Kingdom–United States relations
    • 2026 RAF Fairford arrests
      • The United States Air Force withdraws all of its B-1 Lancer strategic bombers from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England. The U.S. Department of Defense confirms the bombers have returned to bases in the United States. (BBC News)

Law and crime

  • International Criminal Court investigation in Afghanistan
    • The International Criminal Court unseals arrest warrants for Taliban education minister Habibullah Agha and higher education minister Neda Mohammad Nadeem, accusing them of the crime against humanity of gender-based persecution in Afghanistan. (AFP via France 24)
  • Protesters clash with police in Pristina, Kosovo, after parliament fails to advance legislation limiting the Kosovo Specialist Chambers' powers. One police officer and 11 civilians are injured. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • 2025–2026 Kosovo political deadlock
    • In Kosovo, the acting presidency of Albulena Haxhiu becomes de facto due to her having continuously served in the position for more than six months since assuming office on 4 April, violating the third paragraph of Article 90 in the constitution. The Kuvendi has two days left until the presidential election deadline by the Constitutional Court expires. (Kosovo Online) (RKS)
  • 2026 Quebec general election
    • Voters in Quebec, Canada, elect members to the National Assembly. (CBC) (The Guardian)
    • The Parti Québécois is elected into a minority government while the ruling Coalition Avenir Québec face an electoral wipeout. (CBC)
  • 2026 Romanian political crisis
    • Romanian president Nicușor Dan designates diplomat Luca Niculescu to form a government. Niculescu's choice is the fourth attempt by Dan to appoint a Prime Minister to succeed Ilie Bolojan, who lost a no-confidence vote last May. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Spanish general election, 2026 Spanish housing protests
    • Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez calls a snap general election for 29 November after Parliament voted down two emergency housing decrees that would have restricted evictions, frozen rents, and blocked vulture-fund property buys. (The Guardian) (Reuters)
  • The President of Iran, Masoud Pezeshkian, nominates Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi to the post of Defense Minister. (Gulf News)
  • The National Assembly of Laos approves deputy prime minister Saleumxay Kommasith as the new Prime Minister, succeeding Sonexay Siphandone, who became National Assembly president. (The Laotian Times)
  • The House of Peoples' Representatives of Ethiopia reelects Abiy Ahmed as Prime Minister. (Anadolu Agency)

Science and technology

  • American scientist Karl Deisseroth of Stanford University, and German biophysicists Peter Hegemann of Humboldt University and Georg Nagel of the University of Würzburg are jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine for "their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics". (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - October 09, 2026
item.description:
October 9, 2026 (2026-10-09) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • Casualties of the 2026 Iran war
      • The Pentagon raises the U.S. military death toll in the Iran war to 21 after reporting two noncombat deaths. (The Hill)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war, 2026 Blue Nile campaign
      • An RSF drone strike in Blue Nile State, Sudan, kills 41 displaced people. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • Tropical cyclones in 2026
    • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
      • Hurricane Isaias
        • Isaias strengthens into a category 3 Atlantic hurricane. It would later weaken to category 2, with 365,000 people in Alabama and Florida, United States, reported to be without power ahead of its landfall. (AP) (MS Now)
        • Isaias makes landfall near Destin, Florida, and weakens to a category 1 hurricane. (AP) (Reuters via The Straits Times)
    • 2026 Pacific hurricane season
      • Hurricane Rachel
        • Flooding is reported in areas of Southern California, U.S., including Long Beach and Newport Beach, and the National Hurricane Center issues a tropical storm warning for the area. The warning is the first issued for San Diego County, California, since 2023 during Hurricane Hilary. (Los Angeles Times) (KTLA) (KNSD)
      • Hurricane Simon
        • Simon strengthens into a category 2 Pacific hurricane. (AP)
  • 2026 Panama earthquake
    • A magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes Herrera Province, Panama. A nationwide tsunami warning is issued. (Reuters) (USA Today)
  • A passenger bus collides with a truck on a road in Mkambarani, Morogoro Region, Tanzania, and catches fire, killing 28 people. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
    • Eight more children in Bangladesh are reported to be killed from measles, bringing the death toll past 1,155. (BSS)

International relations

  • Montenegro–Russia relations
    • Montenegro expels Russian military blogger Mikhail Zvinchuk and four other Russian nationals on national security grounds after detaining them in Risan. (AFP via RFI)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Musée Renoir theft
    • Six people suspected of stealing Pierre-Auguste Renoir's paintings Young Woman at the Well and Madame Colonna Romano from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer, Alpes-Maritimes, France, are arrested, and the artworks are recovered. (AP) (Reuters)
  • 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
    • South African judge and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "her efforts to promote peace and international law". (DW)
  • Shootings by U.S. immigration agents in the second Trump administration
    • Clashes erupt in New York City, United States, between protestors and police after the shooting of a Dominican Republic national with a criminal conviction by ICE agents. The man, who was in a car alongside a child, was then detained while being wounded. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Erie shooting
    • Eight people are killed, including the perpetrator, in a mass shooting at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, United States. (AP) (BBC News)
  • The Supreme Federal Court of Brazil issues an arrest warrant for Eduardo Bolsonaro, the brother of presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, on charges of lobbying the U.S. to interfere in the trial of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. (Al Jazeera)
  • A man armed with a knife takes 13 children and staff members hostage at a school in Curitiba, Paraná, Brazil, and threatens to set it on fire, before being shot dead by police. The hostages are rescued, with two children sustaining injuries. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • Next Palestinian legislative election
    • Palestinian vice president Hussein al-Sheikh announces that the Palestinian legislative election planned for November 28 will be postponed, possibly until September 2027, along with the also delayed presidential election, because of worsening conditions throughout Palestine. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Czech Senate election, 2026 Czech municipal elections
    • Czechs begin voting in the first round to elect one-third of the Senate. Incumbent prime minister Andrej Babiš seeks gains of his coalition in the Senate. Municipal elections are also underway. (AP)
  • The Mauritanian government of Prime Minister Moctar Ould Diay resigns over power outages. However, President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani reappoints Diay, asking him to form a new government. (AFP via Arab News)
  • Pope Leo XIV approves Filipino cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle's election as dean of the College of Cardinals, making him the first Asian to lead the body that elects a new pope. (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - October 02, 2026
item.description:
October 2, 2026 (2026-10-02) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Yemeni civil war
    • Red Sea crisis
      • 2026 Yemen offensives, Strait of Bab al-Mandab crisis
        • Reuters reports that Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive on the Houthis in the coming weeks to take back the Bab al-Mandab Strait. (Reuters)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • Ethiopian government forces push Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) rebels out of Afar Region after recapturing the towns of Abala, Erebti and Megale. (AFP via France 24)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign
      • Sudan's armed forces announces that they have recaptured the North Kordofan town of al-Mazroub. (Al Jazeera)
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • The death toll in the Rapid Support Forces drone attack on the University of Kordofan in El Obeid rises to 10. (AFP via Arab News)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
      • A Russian drone strikes Pivdennyi Bridge in Kyiv, Ukraine, for the fourth time in two days. (The Kyiv Independent)
  • Boko Haram insurgency
    • Eighteen people are killed as Boko Haram gunmen open fire on villagers collecting firewood in Marte, Borno State, Nigeria. (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
    • The G7 countries announce a plan to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil to combat rising fuel prices caused by the Iran war. (The New York Times)
  • Argentina introduces an immigrant investor program allowing foreigners to obtain citizenship through a US$350,000 contribution to the Ministry of Economy or an $800,000 government bond, with lower additional payments required for spouses and children. (AFP)

Disasters and accidents

  • Twenty people are killed and five others are injured after a four-vehicle crash in Plateau, Nigeria. (Xinhua)
  • The United States National Park Service confirms that the Hōlei Sea Arch, located on Hawaii's Big Island, has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean. (The Guardian)

Law and crime

  • 2026 French lycée protests
    • Mass rioting continues for a third day across France with hundreds reportedly injured and over 735 schools shut, while more than 2,000 people are arrested. (BBC News)
    • Riot police clash with protesters in Paris, Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille as justice minister Gérald Darmanin says protests had "gone from high-school student demonstrations to a public order disturbance" and urges an immediate end to violence. (BBC News)
    • French government ministers, including education minister Édouard Geffray, accuse the far-left of inciting the youth-led unrest across the country. Intelligence agencies briefing the government during a crisis meeting on the riots accuse the left-wing La France Insoumise of actively inciting people to join the protests. (AFP via NDTV) (Ynet News)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Spanish housing protests
    • Spain's parliament rejects two government housing decrees that would have expanded protections against evictions, limited some real-estate practices, encouraged rentals through tax incentives, and allowed tenants to renew residential leases automatically. (AP)
  • 2026 Swiss Federal Council election
    • Swiss president Guy Parmelin announces his resignation from the Federal Council effective December 31. Parliament is expected to elect his successor on 9 December. (AFP) (Swissinfo)
